PRDSection: E3 / SCR-PAY-01, the fr.last_booking_reference table

PRDSection: E3 / P-PAY-01 exception 4, P-PAY-07 exception 4

PRDSection: E2 / P-SEA-06 held_by_me_paying + TAB_REFRESHED, against E3 / SCR-PAY-01

PRDSection: E3 / P-PAY-07, P-PAY-09 exception 7, P-PAY-01 exception 4

PRDSection: E2 / P-HLD-14 rows 2 and 3, against SCR-SEA-01 state "Hold live, further seats chosen"

We are waiting for the answer to your payment. Do not close this page."
WhyItMatters: The screen would navigate away from a request it has just told the customer not to leave, abandoning the response to a confirm that can still capture money and commit a booking, and the customer would land on the seat map with no indication that a booking was made.

PRDSection: E3 / P-PAY-09; E2 / P-HLD-09 and the E2 cross-lane dependency note

PRDSection: E6 S4 P-ADM-03 exception 12
Seam: API -> S3: PutObject refused, allowance exhausted

WhyItMatters: The admin is told to retry an action that can never succeed, and because P-ADM-05 refuses publication without a poster no new film can be published until somebody diagnoses the real cause by hand.

PRDSection: E8 S4 P-XCT-14 unwatched list
Seam: API -> S3: poster object storage

WhyItMatters: The one store in the product with no deletion path at all is the one the operator is never told is unwatched, so it fills silently and first shows up as a failed upload.

PRDSection: E6 S5 SCR-ADM-02 gate copy / E1 EP-BRW-05
Seam: time: display_until reached
Statement: SCR-ADM-02 publishes "Its display window has ended. Customers can no longer see this film." while EP-BRW-05's authorisation rule states that the booking surface does not apply the movie visibility gates.
WhyItMatters: An admin who closes a display window in order to stop a film selling is told it worked, while the showtimes may still be reachable and sellable by direct link.

PRDSection: E6 S6 EP-ADM-10 and EP-ADM-11 / S4 P-ADM-10
Seam: API -> Postgres: showtime insert and update
Statement: EP-ADM-10 and EP-ADM-11 bound base_price_paise at "integer, 1 or more" and carry none of P-ADM-10's arithmetic ceiling, and S1.2 ranks the endpoint block above the P-row on a field bound.

PRDSection: E6 S4 P-ADM-10 and P-ADM-11 / S5 SCR-ADM-03
Seam: API -> Postgres: showtime insert
Statement: No business upper bound exists on base_price_paise or on uplift_basis_points, and the showtime create form carries no confirmation step, unlike the uplift edit which carries one with a blast-radius count.
WhyItMatters: An admin typing 25000 into a rupees field creates a showtime priced a hundred times over in one click, and the customer who pays it cannot be refunded because no refund and no showtime withdrawal exist.

PRDSection: E6 S4 P-ADM-13 validation / E8 P-XCT-30 exception 8
Seam: API -> Postgres: seat insert
Statement: P-XCT-30 forbids the letter I in a seeded seat label because I and 1 are misread on a row marker, and P-ADM-13's row_label bound of one to four letters permits an admin to type it.
WhyItMatters: A hand-laid hall can carry a row I whose label is misread at the door, which is the surface the seed's own rule exists to protect, and P-ADM-14 makes the label permanent.

PRDSection: E8 S4 P-XCT-30 / E6 S4 P-ADM-14
Seam: API -> Postgres: the first showtime row freezes the screen
Statement: The seed creates 720 showtimes across all six halls, which freezes every hall's layout under P-ADM-14, and no row states that running the seed is what closes the window for correcting a seat label.
WhyItMatters: An operator who seeds a database before checking seat labels can never renumber a seat in any hall, which is exactly the deadline OPEN-SEATLABEL-01 carries and nothing warns them of it.

PRDSection: E6 S4 P-ADM-17 / S5 SCR-ADM-06
Seam: operator -> Postgres: an account created outside the application
Statement: No endpoint, screen or navigation item creates an admin account, and the only remaining route is a direct database action that runs outside the router dependency and writes no audit row; no procedure for it is documented anywhere.
WhyItMatters: The change log cannot answer who granted a person the ability to change everything, which is the question SRC-001 section 7.6 puts to the audit trail.

PRDSection: E3 / SCR-PAY-01 states table, Expired row, against its own copy table
Seam: hold TTL 180s expires while SCR-PAY-01 is open
Statement: The Expired state says the countdown stops, the pay action is disabled and the customer is returned to the seat map with the selection re-applied, while the copy table publishes a disabled pay-action label "Hold expired" for the same state; no delay or ordering is given.
WhyItMatters: If the screen navigates away at 0:00 the disabled label and the countdown's own zero-state sentence can never be read, so a developer must guess whether to navigate immediately, after a delay, or only on a customer action.

PRDSection: E2 / P-SEA-02, P-HLD-03, P-HLD-04; S3.8 route inventory
Seam: tab closed with a live hold; application -> Redis lock read
Statement: Closing the tab discards sessionStorage and releases nothing, and no endpoint returns a customer's live holds; holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id} exists server-side and is exposed by nothing, so a returning customer has no way to recover the hold token.
WhyItMatters: Their own held seats render held_by_other and are not tappable, so they cannot re-select them to trigger P-HLD-01 step 4's reuse-the-existing-token path, the ten-seat cap keeps counting those seats against them, and if they try again the product tells them the seats were taken by another customer when the other customer is themselves.

PRDSection: E2 / P-HLD-04 title and behaviour, against E3 / P-PAY-10 post-commit step 13
Seam: API -> Redis, removal of the hold token from holds:user at commit
Statement: P-HLD-04 states that a customer may hold at most ten seats for one showtime, while the count is read only from live holds and P-PAY-10 step 13 deliberately removes the token from that set at commit so the cap stops counting seats the customer now owns.
WhyItMatters: The cap bounds concurrent holds and not what one customer can buy on one showtime, so one customer can buy a whole hall in successive ten-seat bookings; a test transcribed from the row's own wording would assert a per-showtime limit the server does not enforce.

PRDSection: E3 / P-PAY-09 exception 4, SCR-PAY-01 states and copy tables
Seam: API -> Redis token bucket after 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT
Statement: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT returns a Retry-After and a message, SCR-PAY-01 states that no error banner on this screen carries a control, and nothing specifies whether the client retries automatically after Retry-After or waits for the customer to press Pay again.
WhyItMatters: The customer is left on a screen that says a booking is being processed with no specified way to learn the outcome, and every manual press spends a token from a bucket of ten per minute per user even when the response is a replay.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-08 happy path step 2
Seam: door -> API: no endpoint returns a booking to anyone but its owner
Statement: P-TKT-08 has the person at the door compare the reference against the day's bookings by whatever means the venue uses; no endpoint, screen or export in the product returns a showtime's bookings or any booking reference to anyone except the booking's own signed-in owner.
WhyItMatters: The venue cannot tell a real reference from an invented one, so the product's only proof of purchase is unverifiable at the only place it is used.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-08 exception 1
Seam: door -> the venue's process; no product read and no product write
Statement: SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02 accepts that one reference can be presented twice but no document says which party is admitted; a booking is a fixed set of numbered seats, so the exception's both get in is not a reachable outcome, and no audit action exists for the incident.
WhyItMatters: A customer who paid is turned away or loses their seats to whoever arrived first, and nothing in the product records that it happened.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-11; P-TKT-05 happy path step 5
Seam: SES -> the customer's mail provider
Statement: P-TKT-05 sets receipt_dispatch.status to sent when SES accepts the message, while P-TKT-11 states that receipt_dispatch answers whether the customer got their receipt; bounces and complaints publish to SNS and nothing subscribes, so a bounced or spam-filed receipt is recorded as sent.
WhyItMatters: An operator answering a customer who has paid and cannot enter reads sent and concludes the receipt was delivered when the product has no evidence that it was.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-05 happy path step 4
Seam: worker -> SES: SendEmail
Statement: No timeout is specified for the worker's SES call and the S7.9 inventory contains no SES client timeout.
WhyItMatters: A hung SES call leaves the claim in sending, so the receipt cannot be reclaimed by any redelivery until RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS of 900 has elapsed.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-01 happy path step 1
Seam: the customer's screen -> a person's eye or ear at the door
Statement: The reference alphabet excludes 0, 1, I, L, O and U but keeps the confusable pairs 2/Z, 5/S, 8/B and 6/G, and the reference carries no check character; P-TKT-02 correctly refuses to map anything.
WhyItMatters: A single mis-read at the door or over the telephone yields another well-formed reference rather than a detectable error, and references already issued to customers cannot be re-cut.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-05 worked example
Seam: queue -> dead letter queue
Statement: P-TKT-05 states that the deployment specification owes the client the rule that RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS of 900 must exceed the queue's visibility timeout and that maxReceiveCount must exceed eight; docs/30 Deployment/ holds only AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md and its SQS row names neither value.
WhyItMatters: A client who accepts a maxReceiveCount of eight or fewer sends every reclaimable receipt to the dead letter queue before the stale claim can be retaken, and no alarm reports it.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-11; E4 / EP-TKT-02
Seam: operator -> API: no endpoint re-sends a receipt
Statement: EP-TKT-02 is authorised on ownership alone with no override and no admin endpoint re-sends a receipt, so P-TKT-11 names how an operator discovers a failed receipt and gives no way to act on one.
WhyItMatters: An operator who finds a dead-lettered receipt for a paying customer has no product action available and must redrive the queue in the AWS console, which is Zone C and specified nowhere.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-10
Seam: API -> queue -> worker -> SES: password_reset.send
Statement: P-TKT-10's table of the four routes a customer can reach without the email does not state that all four require an authenticated session, nor that the password reset which restores one travels the same outbox, worker and SES path the receipt failed on.
WhyItMatters: A customer at the door who is signed out and has forgotten their password has no route to their reference at all when SES is the failing component.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-06 happy path step 3
Seam: worker -> SES: receipt rendering
Statement: The receipt prints seat labels taken from the unnormalised row_label column, so C12 and c12 render as two seats a person reads as one name, and that label is then read aloud at the door.
WhyItMatters: Two seats sharing one spoken name at the entrance sends two parties to one place, and P-ADM-14 freezes row_label once a showtime exists on the hall.

PRDSection: E4 / SCR-TKT-02; E4 / P-TKT-10
Seam: SES -> the customer's mail provider
Statement: Nothing specifies a verified sending domain, DKIM or SPF for SES_SENDER_ADDRESS, and no bounce or complaint handling exists anywhere.
WhyItMatters: A receipt filed as spam is indistinguishable from one never sent, on the customer's side and the operator's alike, and it is the customer's only way into the hall.

PRDSection: E4 / P-TKT-09; E4 / SCR-TKT-01 states
Seam: browser -> API: GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{reference}
Statement: The receipt's dispatch state is deliberately absent from the customer API, so queued, in flight, delivered and definitively failed render identically on SCR-TKT-01.
WhyItMatters: A customer whose receipt failed presses the resend control blind and can be refused with 202 queued false for a receipt that will never arrive.

PRDSection: E1 / S4 P-BRW-04
Seam: time: listing date strip -> a local day with no showtime

PRDSection: E1 / S4 P-BRW-04 and P-BRW-06; E6 / S4 P-ADM-07
Seam: time: display window boundary against showtime starts_at
Statement: No row requires a showtime's starts_at to fall inside its film's display window, and both browse paths to a date are bounded by that window - the listing strip and next_date_with_showtimes condition 2.
WhyItMatters: A showtime created outside the window has seats and is reachable from no guest browse surface at all, so it can never be found or sold except by a hand-typed URL.

PRDSection: E5 / S5 SCR-ACC-01; E5 / S4 P-ACC-13; E8 SCR-XCT-05
Seam: page: SCR-BRW-03 -> SCR-ACC-01 by the header link rather than the primary action
Statement: fr.pending_selection is written only when the seat map's primary action is pressed, and SCR-ACC-01's success rule sends a caller with no stored selection to the movie listing.
WhyItMatters: A guest who signs in from the header while holding a live selection is returned to the listing with the showtime and the seats gone and no message, from the same screen that returns everyone else to their seats.

PRDSection: E1 / S4 P-BRW-11 exception 4 against E8 SCR-XCT-03 and E1 / S5 SCR-BRW-03
Seam: system: API -> Redis rate-limit bucket, on the first seat-map load

PRDSection: E1 / S6 EP-BRW-06; E8 / S4 P-XCT-07
Seam: system: API -> Redis token bucket, keyed per IP only
Statement: The seat-map read is limited to 120 per minute per IP with no per-user bucket because it is unauthenticated, and no row states what happens when several guests share one public address.

PRDSection: E5 / S4 P-ACC-13 exception 3 against E1 / S4 P-BRW-07 and E2 / S4 P-HLD-14 row 9
Seam: time: sales cut-off passes during the registration detour
Statement: P-ACC-13 exception 3 publishes 'Sales for this showtime have closed.' for a 409 SALES_CLOSED returned by the hold endpoint; P-BRW-07 states in terms that the hold-attempt surface takes P-HLD-14 row 9's body and not that banner.

PRDSection: E1 / S4 P-BRW-04; E1 / S5 SCR-BRW-01
Seam: system: API -> /api/reference while the listing query succeeds
Statement: P-BRW-04 lists a reachable reference endpoint as a precondition and specifies no exception path for it being unreachable; SCR-BRW-01's Error state describes only the listing failing.
WhyItMatters: A reference outage renders as a listing with no filter controls, which the same row says is the correct day-one state, so the guest and the operator cannot tell a working screen from a degraded one.

PRDSection: E7 / S5 SCR-RPT-01 Copy vs E8 S7.19
Seam: page: SCR-RPT-01 period line on every period change
Statement: SCR-RPT-01 publishes the period lines 'Friday 14 August 2026' and 'Monday 10 August to Sunday 16 August 2026', which spell the weekday and month in full and match none of the five date forms S7.19 declares itself the sole owner of.
WhyItMatters: The period line is the manager's only statement of which window the money figures cover, and S7.19's own conformance audit lists five outstanding non-conformances and does not include these, so nothing downstream will catch them.

PRDSection: E8 P-XCT-05 worked example vs E7 P-RPT-09 and api/error_codes.md
Seam: system: POST against the reports router
Statement: P-XCT-05's worked example states 'POST anything on the reports router -> 404, no such route', while P-RPT-09 and the error registry both give 405 for a path that exists under another method.

PRDSection: E7 / S5 SCR-RPT-01 States and Copy
Seam: page: SCR-RPT-01 empty-scope state for a manager with no assignment
Statement: SCR-RPT-01's 'Empty - no halls assigned' state enumerates what renders and what is absent and names neither the scope line nor the hall filter, and the copy table publishes scope-line strings only for a manager with halls and for an administrator.

PRDSection: E8 P-XCT-05 exception table vs E7 P-RPT-01, P-RPT-02 and P-RPT-08
Seam: system: router authorisation refusal on /api/reports
Statement: P-XCT-05 publishes four verbatim strings that differ from the strings P-RPT-01, P-RPT-02 and P-RPT-08 publish for the same four conditions: no session, wrong role, an out-of-scope hall, and an empty scope.
WhyItMatters: Both are rank-2 P-rows about the same router dependency, so S1.2's ranking does not obviously settle which words a manager reads when they are refused a hall, and two of the four pairs are different sentences rather than paraphrases.

PRDSection: E8 P-XCT-05 exception 5 vs E7 P-RPT-09 exception 1
Seam: system: manager request against an /api/admin write endpoint
Statement: P-XCT-05's exception 5 states that a manager reaching any write endpoint 'cannot occur - no write endpoint exists on the manager router', while P-RPT-09 specifies 403 FORBIDDEN with published copy for exactly that request against the administration router.
WhyItMatters: A developer building the authorisation floor from E8 alone would write no test for a manager calling an admin write path, because the floor row says the case is impossible, and that is the single case SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 exists to prevent.

PRDSection: E6 P-ADM-17 vs S3.6 and api/contract.json
Seam: system: manager session against EP-HLD-01, EP-HLD-03, EP-HLD-04, EP-PAY-01, EP-TKT-02
Statement: P-ADM-17 states 'a manager writes nothing, ever', while S3.6's capability matrix grants a manager hold and pay and the generated contract admits the manager role on five non-GET endpoints.
WhyItMatters: A manager can create a booking in a hall whose takings they report on, so the sentence a reviewer would check the product against is false, and the money that manager spends lands inside the figure they are the reader of.

PRDSection: E6 P-ADM-09 vs E7 P-RPT-01 and P-RPT-05
Seam: time: a booked showtime's movie_id or starts_at edited between two dashboard reads
Statement: P-ADM-09 states that editing a showtime which already has bookings 'changes nothing about them' and protects seat_count_at_creation and the seat set from recomputation while leaving movie_id and starts_at editable, and P-RPT-05 joins movie_id live and P-RPT-01 filters on starts_at live.
WhyItMatters: A period a manager already read and acted on can change film attribution and total takings after the fact - on the worked example a day's takings fall from 2783331 paise to 300000 and occupancy from 29.5 per cent to 5.5 per cent - which R-RPT-04 forbids.

PRDSection: E7 P-RPT-11 and SCR-RPT-01 States
Seam: page: manager reaches /dashboard/audit and is refused
Statement: No surface tells a manager that a figure changed or why: the dashboard is recomputed live with nothing precomputed, and the change log that records the administrator edit is admin-only with no link in a manager's DOM.
WhyItMatters: A manager who reported a number yesterday and sees a different one today has no route to an explanation and cannot distinguish an administrator's correction from a fault in the dashboard, which is the state P-RPT-07 says makes a reader stop trusting the figures.

PRDSection: E7 P-RPT-02 and P-RPT-01; E6 P-ADM-17
Seam: time: a manager assigned today stepping the period backwards without bound
Statement: A manager_screen_assignment row carries no validity period and P-RPT-01 places no lower or upper bound on the anchor date, so a manager assigned this morning reads that hall's entire financial history and its future advance sales, and an unassigned manager loses all of it silently.
WhyItMatters: Who may see the business's money and for which periods is a decision about financial access that no frozen source, client ruling or APPROVED record answers, and nothing on the screen discloses that the scope has no time bound.

PRDSection: E6 P-ADM-17 happy path step 4
Seam: process: manager creation writes no outbox row and triggers no SES send
Statement: P-ADM-17 creates a manager account with no usable password and specifies no notification of any kind, and the password-reset flow it points at is self-initiated by someone who already knows an account exists at their address.
WhyItMatters: A created manager account is unreachable until a human tells the manager out of band, and P-ACC-08 confirms the reset path is the only way such an account ever signs in for the first time, so a silent creation produces an account nobody can use.

PRDSection: E6 S5 SCR-ADM-01 Partial state
Seam: API -> S3: presigned GET URL, one hour
Statement: A film whose poster object cannot be fetched renders the same empty box and the same words "No poster" as a draft that has none, so an expired one-hour presigned URL or an S3 outage is indistinguishable from a missing poster.
WhyItMatters: The admin's remedy for a missing poster is to upload another one, which writes a second permanent object to a bucket nothing ever deletes from.

PRDSection: E6 S4 P-ADM-19 exceptions 1-3 / E8 S4 P-XCT-03 exceptions 1 and 3
Seam: API -> Postgres: the audit insert fails
Statement: Three different verbatim sentences are published for the audit-insert failure; E6 publishes "Something went wrong and nothing was saved..." and E8 publishes both "That change was not saved. Try again." and "The server could not complete this request...".
WhyItMatters: An implementer must pick one, and the PRD's own rule is that a new variant of an existing sentence is a defect rather than a refinement.

PRDSection: E6 S4 P-ADM-19 exception 2 / E8 S4 P-XCT-03 exception 4
Seam: API -> Postgres: audit action vocabulary check
Statement: E6 says a write carrying an action outside the controlled vocabulary rolls the transaction back, while E8 says the check runs at the boundary before the transaction opens.
WhyItMatters: The two describe different code, and only one of them makes a partially-applied change impossible by construction rather than by rollback.

PRDSection: E3 / SCR-PAY-01 states table; E2 / P-HLD-14 row 10; E1 / P-BRW-07 exception 1
Seam: sales cut-off passes while SCR-PAY-01 is open
Statement: SCR-PAY-01 publishes no sales-closed state and no banner, and runs no poll, while SCR-SEA-01 publishes a banner for the same event and P-BRW-07 exception 1 specifies that the seat map's poll surfaces it.
WhyItMatters: A customer whose cut-off passes mid-checkout is shown nothing at all, which is harmless because the confirm does not re-check the cut-off, but the silence is nowhere stated as deliberate and the next reader is as likely to add the banner as to leave it out.

PRDSection: E7 / S5 SCR-RPT-01 Copy, period line week
Seam: time: an ISO week spanning a year boundary
Statement: The week period line has one published form, 'Monday 10 August to Sunday 16 August 2026', which carries a single year at the end, and an ISO week running from 29 December 2025 to 4 January 2026 has no published form.
WhyItMatters: The rendered line puts both dates under one year, so once a year the manager is told the takings cover a week that is twelve months from the one they are reading.
